mainEntity.name: Can AI remove filler words, silence, and mistakes from my talking-head videos without making me sound weird?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI can remove filler words and silences, but aggressive cleanup can make a speaker sound rushed or unnatural. Begin with a transcript-based rough cut, mark essential pauses, and listen to the result at normal speed before applying global edits. Keep a copy of the original recording so you can restore context, tone, or a useful hesitation. For educational or sales content, clarity matters more than removing every pause because pacing affects comprehension and trust. Run My AI Business workflows can include a review checkpoint after transcript editing and another after audio enhancement. Use a short sample to compare naturalness, intelligibility, and total editing time before applying the settings to a series.
acceptedAnswer.description: Often, but not perfectly. Review transcript edits and listen for clipped meaning, unnatural pacing, missing emphasis, and abrupt audio changes. Keep the original recording, preserve useful pauses, and test settings on a short sample before applying them across a course, newsletter, or video series.
